First thing to be said is that this game works really bad on modern RTX cards since the first thing you notice is that skybox and light is flickering. The FPS is kinda low and doesn't change with different presets. So you need to install mods to make it work properly!
From cold Chicago we go to sunny San Francisco. The game changes its tone and it seems both in story and gameplay.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3824930027
The story now feels less serious and depressing which is not bad but also more global. Now we follow not only revenge but we change society. In the first game you was following Aiden's storyline but here I can highlight DedSec as a main character. Marcus in just a part of something bigger while he is still controlled by player. There are several characters that Marcus works and each of them has their own style and attributes that are memorable. 
The game itself is a satire on modern society with AI and Big Brother that is watching your every step which is aged well and actual in 2026.
Gameplaywise this game has better hacking and world interaction than the previous one. Now we can use RC and Drone to solve different riddles and neutralise enemies. Now you can make different gangs fight each other or even call cops on someone you don't like just by getting skill in a skilltree. In this game you have different approach to your enemies: you can hack them through cameras, use drone or RC, just shoot or use environment to neutralise them. 
Also interactions with the world are cool and npcs react on your actions.
One of my favourite things are hacking riddles - there are plenty of them during the story and on the map and many of them make you think.
To be honest shooting is not the strongest part of the game. You don't have slow motion like in the first game and you don't really feel the impact of the guns.
Visuals are incredible sometimes the game looks very realistic and thats the 2016 game!!!

Not my favorite game from the series but definitely not the worst one. It looks good, I like how San Francisco looks and how huge it is (it brings me GTA SA memories) and I love the inclusion of drones and car hacks. Of course it has some few missteps I wanna mention.
First, I wanna talk about the story and the characters. I liked the 1st WatchDogs because of its darker tone and more grounded story, not saying that making a more light-hearted story isn't good but I don't feel like WD takes much advantage with this. DedSec's whole motivation of helping people see the corruption is obviously the whole point of the group but it just doesn't feel as impactful or important as they try to make it sound. It becomes uninteresting pretty quick and it doesn't help that Blume and Dusan don't feel like a threat at all during a big chunk of the story and Dusan's appearance as the villains was too obvious during the first minutes of the game. As I just mentioned, Dusan isn't as threatening like Lucky Quinn or Damien for example, even though Ubi tries from time to time to make him look calculated and "unpredictable", all that stuff. The DedSec group isn't fleshed out either. The only one who feels somewhat interesting is Wrench but even he gets beaten up by the writing. Horatio gets killed in one operation and never mourned, nor mentioned ever again throughout the game just because Ubi didn't know how to do with him and T-Bone gets sidelined like crazy and he looks more like a cameo character that deserved to be in a side operation instead. I swear, Clara would laugh off just to see the people who formed DedSec in the first place.
Lastly I wanna talk about some other stuff that I didn't like as much about the game: The money you can make feels nerfed compared to WD1, no upgrades regarding that whatsoever. Sure you have in-game activities that give you money like ridesharing and time trials but they still give you so less. It's like GTA5 all over again. Another thing I didn't like would be the lack of "research" points. Sure, those are scattered around the map but I just finished the game and I still couldn't complete every single nod. Maybe if the upgrade costs were lowered. And speaking of upgrades, I mentioned I like introduction of drones and "rc cars" and car hacks but I also like the fact that we have almost unlimited gadgets, although in a smaller number (only electros shocks, bombs and Blackouts) but why is Blackout useless in this game? Outside of multiplayer, the coolest "ability" in the game gets zero use. Also what happened to ctOS scans after heavy cop chases and the signal jammers? Welp, at least those are getting replaced by a little broken detection system by the enemies and again, car hacks.
I'm not saying WatchDogs 2 is BAD, bad (unlike Legion) but not good either. Just below the first game. And whoever wants to play this game I welcome you.

Originally played on the PS4 back in 2016, but now there couldn't be a better time to play this game. Especially with all the technology invading privacy nowadays, social media being used to distort people's views, or divide people, corruption in government and corporations, all that stuff. I also LOVE the more light-heartedness of this game, I don't care what anyone else says. I love the characters, the tone, the settings, and all. 

As mentioned by a lot of people, this game is a great open world sandbox too. There's A LOT of creativity in how you can approach a mission or enemy territories. All the gadgets you get, tools, hacks, weapons, all make for a great variety. You can go pure stealth no kills, spam distract and sneak by, spam black outs, hack cars to run enemies over, go on a mayhem and kill everyone, melee takedowns only, non-lethal only, drive explosives into enemies, drop bombs on enemies with the quadcopter, etc. SO SO many options it is genuinely so fun changing your approach each time. 

Also still the most alive feeling open world game I've played to date. I feel less inclined to murder random npcs on the street because of that, same with enemies. There's unique events that happen everywhere in the game, and every npc has a unique profile to them. I'm a Bay Area citizen and they absolutely nailed how San Francisco looks and it's vibes. I couldn't be more happy with it, this game was a gift to me.

Watch_Dogs 2 is a third person open world action/stealth game that takes the few things that were good about the first Watch_Dogs and pumps them up to 11.

The game controls great, the free running is much more fluid, there's tons more side content and just general stuff to do. San Fransisco looks beautiful and it's actually insane how good this game still looks 10 years after release.

The city is more vibrant and has more interesting locales than Watch_Dogs 1 and is really fun to roam around in and find stuff. It reminded me why the "Ubisoft open world" got so popular in the first place - when it's done well, it's a really fun playground!

One of my biggest gripes about Watch_Dogs 1 was the overly edgy writing - this has been toned down in the sequel, albeit it's been replaced with what some might call "millenial cringe". Personally, I found it fun - a real time-capsule of the mid 2010s. The cast is fun and all the personalities are interesting without becoming grating caricatures

Another thing they really improved on in the second game is the stealth. You now have actual options for it and just mowing down a whole compound of enemies is reasonably harder than in the first game. The quadcopter and jumper provide a lot of versatility for approaching encounters and there were some missions that to my great glee I managed to complete without ever setting foot in the restricted area

All in all, if you miss the days when open worlds were cool instead of tiring busy-work, then I suggest getting this game on sale! It's great fun

Watch Dogs 2 is a pretty decent game and I had a good time playing it, but I wouldn't call it anything special. The story is okay, the characters are interesting enough, and the open world is fun to explore at first, but the game has quite a few problems that keep it from being great.

One of the best things about the game is definitely the main missions. There are some genuinely fun moments, and Robot Wars was easily my favorite mission in the entire game. It was creative, entertaining, and actually felt different from the usual missions. Unfortunately, most of the other missions follow pretty much the same formula: break into a building, hack something, get the information you need, and leave. The hacking itself is fun initially, especially when you use drones and different gadgets to avoid enemies, but it gets repetitive after a while. I really wish there were more types of hacking mechanics and more variety in how you approach objectives.

I also tried a few side missions, but honestly, most of them were pretty trash and didn't really motivate me to keep playing them. The open world has plenty of activities, but quantity doesn't always mean quality.

The characters are decent, and Ray was easily my favorite. He has a lot of personality and brings some entertaining moments to the story. Dusan, on the other hand, reminded me a bit of Joseph Seed from Far Cry 5, both in appearance and behavior. The story itself is okay, but I never found it particularly amazing or memorable.

Driving isn't bad either, and the cars handle well enough, but I barely used them because fast travel was simply more convenient. I honestly don't think I've ever gone somewhere without using fast travel unless a mission forced me to drive. The city looks great, though, and exploring San Francisco is enjoyable, especially with all the hacking opportunities and things you can interact with.

I also like that the game gives you different ways to approach certain situations. You can sneak around, use your gadgets, distract enemies, or go in more aggressively if things go wrong. Playing stealthily and using your tools creatively can be really satisfying, even if the underlying objectives start feeling repetitive.

Overall, Watch Dogs 2 is worth playing, especially if you enjoy open-world games and messing around with hacking mechanics. It has some great moments, likable characters, and a fun setting, but the repetitive missions and underwhelming side content hold it back. It's a good enough game, just not one I'd consider particularly memorable.

For me, the first Watch Dogs is still clearly superior, especially in terms of story, atmosphere, and the overall experience. Watch Dogs 2 is more colorful and playful, but I personally prefer the darker tone of the original.

Final verdict: 7/10. A fun game that's worth trying, but it could have been so much better with more mission variety and a stronger story.

[h3] A Different Side of Watch Dogs [/h3]

Watch Dogs 2 is one of those games that makes you appreciate how much personality an open world can have. Coming back to the series after the first game, it's interesting to see how different the sequel feels while still keeping what made the original enjoyable. San Francisco is a fantastic setting, full of life, colour and things to discover. Exploring the city never really gets old, and the soundtrack fits the atmosphere brilliantly, giving the game its own identity and making the world feel alive. One of my favourite parts is the story and the DedSec crew. The characters each have their own personalities, and their interactions bring plenty of humour and charm. Although the tone is much lighter than the first game, the story still explores interesting ideas about privacy, surveillance and the power of technology. It makes you want to see what happens next. The gameplay is another highlight. The hacking mechanics give you plenty of freedom in how you approach missions, while the RC Jumper and Quadcopter make things even more enjoyable. Experimenting with different approaches keeps the gameplay fresh throughout. Of course, the game isn't perfect. Some of the humour doesn't always land, and parts of the story feel a little uneven, but these issues don't take away from the overall experience. Overall, Watch Dogs 2 is a brilliant sequel that takes the series in a different direction and makes it work. With a memorable cast, an incredible setting and entertaining gameplay, it's a game that's easy to get lost in. It may feel very different from the original, but that's exactly what makes it stand out.
